audit_findings.title: Facet creates a post-close claim/perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $828.7 million cash consideration; approximately $820.0 million new debt at 4.6%, implying approximately $37.7 million annual pre-tax interest; post-close long-term debt approximately $1.4 billion
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor excludes Facet earnings and acquisition-related costs, while the cash bridge and equity-level OE exclude the post-close cash use and debt interest.
audit_findings.evidence: Acquisitions, joint ventures and strategic investments could negatively impact our profitability and financial condition due to operating and integration inefficiencies, the incurrence of debt, contingent liabilities and amortization of expenses related to intangible assets.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error: the September 5 valuation represents a post-close common-equity claim using pre-close operations and balance sheet amounts. Facet earnings would increase OE, while interest, integration costs, purchase accounting and cash consumed would reduce value. The $37.7 million computed annual interest alone is 13.5% of the $279 million anchor, and Facet's earnings are unknown, so the net direction is mixed but clearly capable of materially changing intrinsic value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the valuation from the first post-close filing, using post-close cash, debt and shares, and reconcile Facet earnings, approximately $37.7 million annual interest, integration costs, purchase accounting and closing cash flows into equity-level OE.

audit_findings.title: Contingent acquisition payments are an unbridged claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.5 million recorded liability and $21.5 million maximum payout at April 30, 2026; $6.2 million FY2025 fair-value reduction; maximum payout equals approximately $0.18 per share and 0.44%-0.60% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Uncaptured settlement payments overstate the equity bridge, and any nonrecurring liability-remeasurement gain retained in anchor OE overstates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum potential payout of the contingent consideration was $ 22.5 million and $ 29.8 million as of July 31, 2025 and July 31, 2024, respectively, see Note 18.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted claim is demonstrated, although retention of the remeasurement gain in the $279 million OE anchor is unresolved. Even conservatively treating the full $6.2 million reduction as recurring OE and adding the $21.5 million maximum claim produces an approximate $95-$124 million total sensitivity, or $0.78-$1.02 per share and about 2.5%-2.7% of scenario equity value. That scale cannot bridge the $50.97-$61.66 gap between the $91.03 price and the $29.37-$40.06 valuation range, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the post-Facet recorded and maximum liabilities, deduct any settlement claim outside OE, and rerun the anchor after removing any contingent-consideration remeasurement gain actually retained in OE.

audit_findings.title: Receivables factoring may inflate cash-based owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 factoring cash proceeds were $82.0 million versus $28.2 million in FY2024, a $53.8 million increase equal to 19.3% of the $279 million anchor; full adjustment sensitivity is approximately $640-$892 million of operating value, or $5.23-$7.30 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Factoring proceeds classified in operating cash flow can reduce the reported receivables investment and inflate cash-based OE without increasing underlying customer earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: Cash received from selling receivables in fiscal 2025 and 2024 of $ 82.0 million and $ 28.2 million, respectively, is presented as a change in accounts receivable within the operating section of the Consolidated Statements of Cash Flow.
audit_findings.explanation: The operating-cash-flow classification and $53.8 million year-over-year increase are demonstrated; whether the OE computation neutralized them is unresolved. If untreated, the increase is large relative to the anchor and could materially alter intrinsic value and the buy-below threshold, even though its downward direction would reinforce the conclusion that the shares are expensive at $91.03.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 OE to operating cash flow and receivables sold, calculate OE before factoring, apply one consistent treatment to every historical year, retain the $4.1 million FY2025 factoring cost, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Equity-method holdings are not visibly reconciled between OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $109.2 million aggregate carrying amount at April 30, 2026 versus $67.9 million added to the bridge, leaving $41.3 million unreconciled; nine-month equity earnings were $7.2 million, including $10.1 million from AFSI before other affiliate results
audit_findings.mechanism: Affiliate value may be omitted from the bridge or counted twice if the related after-interest earnings remain in OE while standalone stake value is also added.
audit_findings.evidence: The aggregate carrying amount of these investments was $ 103.6 million and $ 26.9 million as of July 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The numerical mismatch is demonstrated, but it does not establish an error because the $67.9 million may represent only Medica while AFSI and PTPJM are intentionally valued through earnings retained in OE. The $41.3 million balance difference is approximately $0.34 per share and 1.0% of base equity value, but the treatment and capitalization of affiliate earnings are not shown, so the record cannot bound the complete valuation effect or determine its direction.
audit_findings.action: Prepare an investment-by-investment schedule for Medica, AFSI and PTPJM showing carrying value, standalone bridge value, distributions and earnings included in OE; then rerun after assigning each holding to either OE or the bridge, never both.

audit_findings.title: The latest-year anchor may retain a nonrecurring impairment
audit_findings.magnitude: $62.0 million pre-tax impairment, equal to 22.2% of the $279 million anchor; if fully retained, linear operating-value sensitivity is approximately $738-$1,028 million, or $6.03-$8.41 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Retention depresses anchor OE as though the noncash impairment recurs annually; removing it without adjusting growth or reinvestment assumptions can overstate value by ignoring the demonstrated acquisition underperformance.
audit_findings.evidence: As a result of the valuation, the Company recorded $ 62.0 million of impairment expense related to intangible assets in the Company’s bioprocessing businesses within the Life Sciences segment during the third quarter of fiscal 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The impairment is demonstrated, but its inclusion in the OE anchor is unresolved because no OE reconciliation was supplied. Its size makes the issue material if any substantial portion remains. The direction is mixed: mechanical exclusion increases value, while the underlying evidence of weaker bioprocessing demand and acquisition returns may justify lower growth or returns on reinvestment.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $62.0 million charge through the exact FY2025 OE calculation, exclude any amount treated as a recurring cash expense, document the tax effect, and separately rerun growth and reinvestment assumptions to reflect the disclosed operating deterioration.

audit_findings.title: The AFSI guarantee is an off-balance-sheet contingent claim
audit_findings.magnitude: AFSI debt was $37.5 million at April 30, 2026; DCI's 50% guarantee was approximately $18.75 million, or $0.15 per share and 0.38%-0.52% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A guarantee payment would be an equity claim outside ordinary after-interest OE and would reduce the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The outstanding debt relating to AFSI, of which the Company guarantees half, was $ 43.9 million and $ 51.0 million as of July 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantee exposure is demonstrated, but the presently filed maximum attributable amount is small relative to the $3.591-$4.897 billion scenario equity values. Even assuming a full $18.75 million payment with no recovery, it would reduce value by only about $0.15 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion. Loss of AFSI earnings in a failure scenario would be a separate operating issue.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the current guaranteed balance, collateral, cross-default provisions and AFSI coverage; monitor for deterioration and rerun only if the guaranteed amount grows materially or AFSI's earnings and asset coverage weaken.
